rationale: C24 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both are resignation-acceptance letters that open with regret and an effective date, explain that the departing official is leaving to pursue electoral public service, review the official's contributions, and recast the departure as continued service to the country. This candidacy-related structure is substantially more distinctive than the generic resignation-and-praise pattern in C25 or C09. The wording is not unusually close, so the relationship is principally structural and functional rather than literal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I accept your resignation as the Representative of the United States to the United Nations and to the Security Council, effective, as you wish, September third.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is with profound personal regret that I accept your resignation as Secretary of the Interior, effective April fifteenth.
shared_material.explanation: Both use a formal acceptance of resignation coupled with regret, the office being vacated, and a specified effective date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The deep regret I feel at contemplating your leaving your United Nations post is mitigated by the knowledge that you do so only to offer yourself to the nation in an elective post of high responsibility and opportunity for service.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: While I am reluctant to forego your valuable assistance as a member of the Cabinet, I understand your purpose and I salute your determination to bring the facts pertaining to this Administration before your fellow citizens of Oregon.
shared_material.explanation: Each pivots from regret at losing the official to approval of the official's departure for an electoral undertaking.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The country could ill afford in these times to lose the service of a man of your abilities.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have no doubt that it will continue to be of benefit to your State and the nation in the years to come.
shared_material.explanation: Both close the substantive discussion by presenting the electoral transition as a continuation of valuable public service.
